approval.cost: No fee for connected apps or PATs is stated anywhere in the documentation read
approval.trigger: Vendor (Tableau) review: none documented. Tableau's documentation describes no app review, no approval process, no marketplace listing, and no partner program for connected apps or PATs; there is nothing to submit to Tableau. The approval is the CUSTOMER's own Tableau administrator: the site admin creates and enables the connected app inside that customer's own site (and, for PATs, the individual user creates the token). Each customer site is a separate setup; there is no cross-customer app. Caps stated: 'You can generate a total of two secrets for each connected app. The second secret can be used for secret rotation purposes.' For PATs on Tableau Server: 'A user can have up to 10 PATs.'
approval.wait: None (no vendor review exists; setup completes as soon as the customer's admin creates the app and hands over the credentials)

blockers.detail: A site admin in EACH customer organization must create the connected app and securely hand the secret to the SaaS. There is no self-serve 'Connect Tableau' OAuth redirect a user can complete alone, and docs prescribe no transfer mechanism for the credentials.
blockers.howToClear: Build an admin-guided onboarding flow (step-by-step instructions for the customer's site admin) and a secure credential intake.
blockers.title: Per-customer, per-site manual setup

blockers.detail: 'For security purposes, a connected app is set to disabled by default when created.' Until the admin explicitly enables it, it does nothing.
blockers.howToClear: Include the enable step prominently in the admin onboarding instructions.
blockers.title: Disabled by default

blockers.detail: Only REST API methods that support JWT authorization can be called this way: 'If a scope is not listed in the method's properties block, access to that method can't be controlled by a JWT.' For Metadata API workflows 'the only supported scope is tableau:content:read'; for VizQL Data Service workflows the only supported scope is tableau:viz_data_service:read.
blockers.howToClear: Check each method's properties block for JWT scope support before designing features on it.
blockers.title: JWT scope coverage is partial

alternatives: Connected App with OAuth 2.0 trust (the customer's own External Authorization Server, e.g. their IdP, issues the JWT and Tableau validates it against the EAS's keys; requires the EAS to be configured and registered first)
Personal Access Token (per-user token name + secret used in REST API Sign In; simpler but unscoped: the session 'has the same access and privileges as the PAT owner')
Username/password Sign In (documented but weakest; not viable where MFA is enabled, see Blockers-adjacent note in Nuances)
flavor.recommended: A Connected App with Direct Trust, created per customer site, used for REST API authorization
flavor.why: There is no Tableau-operated third-party 'OAuth app' registry and no Tableau-hosted consent flow. A Connected App is a per-site trust configuration created inside a customer's Tableau Cloud site or Tableau Server site, with a client ID and up to two secrets (each with a secret ID and secret value). With Direct Trust, the external application signs a JWT with the connected app's shared secret (HS256). Tableau's own framing: 'using Tableau connected apps, you can programmatically call and access the Tableau REST API through your custom application on behalf of Tableau Cloud users. Access to the REST API is enabled by a JSON Web Token (JWT) defined as part of the initial Sign In request.' The SaaS mints a short-lived JWT per user (the sub claim names the Tableau user) with least-privilege scp scopes and exchanges it at the REST API Sign In endpoint for a credentials token.

humanMust: (Customer's Tableau site admin) Create the connected app in the customer's site (Settings > Connected Apps > New Connected App > Direct Trust)
(Customer's Tableau site admin) Enable the connected app (it is disabled by default)
(Customer's Tableau site admin) Generate a secret and hand off the client ID + secret ID + secret value to the SaaS out-of-band
name: Tableau
nuances: Token figures (all provider-stated): JWT maximum validity is ten minutes ('The expiry time (in UTC) of the JWT must be within the maximum validity period, which is ten minutes'; on Tableau Server with OAuth 2.0 trust the maximum can be configured via vizportal.oauth.external_authorization_server.max_expiration_period_in_minutes). Connected app secrets 'do not expire, and remain valid until deleted'. The REST sign-in credentials token 'has a time limit, typically 2 hours' per the REST API tutorial. PATs expire if not used after 15 consecutive days (Cloud: thereafter per the site setting; Server: after one year if used more frequently).

JWT construction details: header kid = secret ID, iss = client ID, alg = HS256 (the only supported algorithm); claims sub = Tableau username (email address on Tableau Cloud), aud = 'tableau' (for OAuth 2.0 trust on Tableau Cloud, aud must be 'tableau:<site_luid>'), exp, jti, and scp = list of access scopes (e.g. tableau:content:read, tableau:datasources:update; 'Do not use scope'). All subsequent REST requests with the credentials token (X-Tableau-Auth header) are bounded by the JWT scopes and the named user's own permissions.

Clock skew kills the trust: 'In order for the session token to be valid, the clocks of the external application and the server that hosts the external application must be set to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).' Licensing constraint: 'you must generate a JWT dynamically for each enabled user. Never embed the credentials for one user in your connected app and then use that as authorization for others.' Secret rotation is manual but dual-slot: deleting a secret invalidates JWTs signed with it.

PAT traps: the secret is shown exactly once ('There is no way to retrieve a secret after that Personal Access Token dialog is closed'); 'Users must create their own PATs. Administrators cannot create PATs for users'; 'PATs are automatically revoked when a user's authentication method is changed'; 'Users can't request concurrent Tableau Cloud sessions with a PAT' (signing in again terminates the previous session). MFA blocker: 'You must use a PAT, instead of user name and password, to make a REST API sign in request to Tableau Cloud with multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled with Tableau authentication.' Embedding-only restrictions (domain allowlist, project access level) do not restrict REST API authorization.
prerequisites: A customer Tableau site admin willing to create and enable the connected app
A secure way to receive and store the per-customer client ID + secret ID + secret value
Server clocks set to UTC (required for JWT validity)

steps.detail: Tableau Cloud: Settings > Connected Apps > New Connected App > Direct Trust (also available via the Tableau REST API connected apps methods). For REST API authorization workflows, only a name is required; Access level and Domain allowlist can be ignored (they are embedding-only). Then enable the app: 'a connected app is set to disabled by default when created'.

steps.title: (Customer site admin) Create and enable the connected app

steps.detail: 'Select the Generate New Secret button. Make note of the secret ID and secret value.' Hand the client ID, secret ID, and secret value to the SaaS out-of-band; the SaaS stores them as its per-customer credential. Up to two secrets per app enable rotation.
steps.title: (Customer site admin) Generate a secret; hand off credentials

steps.detail: JWT header: kid = secret ID, iss = client ID, alg = HS256. Claims: sub = Tableau username (email on Cloud), aud = 'tableau', exp (within the 10-minute maximum validity), jti, scp = list of access scopes. POST /api/{version}/auth/signin with the JWT; the response returns a credentials token, site ID (LUID), and user ID.
steps.title: Mint a JWT per user; exchange at Sign In

steps.detail: Send the credentials token as the X-Tableau-Auth header. Requests are bounded by the scopes in the JWT and by the named user's own Tableau permissions. Re-sign-in when the credentials token expires (typically 2 hours).
steps.title: Call the REST API

steps.detail: Create a PAT on the user's My Account Settings page (the secret is shown once; users must create their own PATs, admins cannot). Sign in via the REST API with the PAT name + secret to get the same credentials token. Suitable only where a customer accepts an unscoped, full-privilege credential.
steps.title: Alternative: PAT sign-in

tagline: Tableau runs no third-party OAuth app program: the 'app' is a Connected App trust config that each customer's site admin creates inside their own site, whose shared secret signs per-user JWTs (10-minute maximum validity) exchanged at REST Sign In. No vendor review exists; the customer's admin is the approval.

time.active: ~15 min of customer-admin setup per site + ~1-2 hrs of JWT code
time.total: Same day per customer (no vendor wait at all)
